content.title: 'Bachelorette' Season Canceled Over Video; Insiders Say Taylor Frankie Paul's Season Could Still Air
content.text: Key PointsABC pulled Taylor Frankie Paul’s Bachelorette season due to a controversial video.Financial and contractual pressures may encourage ABC or Warner Bros. to eventually air the season.The decision is labeled temporary, leaving open the possibility of a future broadcast. Even after ABC pulled Taylor Frankie Paul’s season of The Bachelorette at the last minute, insiders say the show may not be gone for good. According to a new report from Variety, there are strong financial and logistical reasons that the network—and the studio behind the series—may still find a way to air the season in some form.Read More Related: Why Was Taylor Frankie Paul Arrested? Inside the ‘Bachelorette’ Star’s 2023 Assault Case Why ‘The Bachelorette’ Might Still Air One of the biggest factors: money. Sources told Variety that ABC could lose tens of millions of dollars if the season never airs, including licensing fees paid to Warner Bros. Unscripted Television, marketing costs and lost advertising revenue. And while ABC made the call to pull the show, it doesn’t actually own it. Warner Bros. Television Group produces The Bachelorette and distributes it internationally, meaning the studio still has a vested interest in the season being seen somewhere—even if that’s not on ABC’s original schedule. Insiders say Warner Bros. executives are currently taking a “wait-and-see” approach, remaining in contact with ABC as both sides figure out next steps. Related: How Many Kids Does Taylor Frankie Paul Have? Meet the ‘Bachelorette’ Star’s 3 Children YesYes27%NoNo73% What Could Happen Next At this point, multiple outcomes are still on the table. According to Variety, Taylor’s season could still eventually air: on a delay later this year as part of ABC’s summer schedule or potentially on another platform, such as Hulu The season had already completed filming and was intended to serve as a reboot of sorts for the franchise, which has not aired The Bachelorette since 2024. Because of that, shelving it entirely would represent not just a financial loss, but a setback in the franchise’s broader reset. Related: What Is ‘Secret Lives of Mormon Wives’? Inside the MomTok Swinging Scandal That Made Taylor Frankie Paul Famous Why ABC Pulled the Show ABC’s decision came after TMZ released a 2023 video involving Taylor and her estranged partner, Dakota Mortensen. In a statement to Parade, the network said, “In light of the newly released video just surfaced today, we have made the decision to not move forward with the new season of The Bachelorette at this time, and our focus is on supporting the family.” The wording—“at this time”—has become a key detail, as it leaves open the possibility that the decision is not permanent. Taylor Frankie Paul Responds Following ABC’s decision, Taylor released a statement through a spokesperson addressing the situation and the video that surfaced. “Taylor is very grateful for ABC’s support as she prioritizes her family’s safety and security,” the statement reads, adding that she has “silently suffer[ed] extensive mental and physical abuse as well as threats of retaliation.” The statement also claims Taylor is now “gaining the strength to face her accuser” and is “taking steps to ensure that she and her children are protected from any further harm.” It concludes by saying she is “exploring all of her options” and preparing to share her story publicly. Parade has reached out to ABC for additional clarification, including whether Taylor would still be paid for her season if it does not air, but has not yet received a response.
